recommendation: Keep this no-change audit as-is. Revisit only if the work group opens a broader issue to standardize terminology such as "URL escaping" versus "URL encoding" throughout the search page.
issue_request: FHIR-3190 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core search issue asking that the number search parameter page stop saying that "=" must be "escaped"; the reporter clarified that URL percent-encoding, if mentioned at all, should be called URL encoding and not FHIR search escaping.
initial_application: Jira comments record svn revision 3073. In git, commit 568cbc1cc3 changed the DSTU source/search.html number section from "= must be escaped" to "= must be URL-encoded", matching the published correction.
additional_context: Commit 9c1436dab4 later moved ordered search comparisons to textual prefixes such as lt, le, gt, ge, and ne, removing the old symbolic comparison examples and the need for the old "=" encoding reminder. The current source/search.html number section uses textual prefix examples. A newer URL-Encoding note and remaining URL escaping references concern general percent-encoding for URL characters, not the erroneous number-parameter "=" sentence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scoped search page already avoids saying that "=" must be escaped in number searches.
